# JavaScript — understand state and execution order

## 1. Primitive values versus object references

~~~js
const a = { n: 3 };
const b = a;
b.n = 7;
console.log(a.n); // 7
~~~

The variables refer to the same object. Reassigning b to a different object would not reassign a. For a separate shallow copy use an object spread, but nested objects can remain shared.

## 2. A closure remembers an outer binding

~~~js
function counter() {
  let n = 0;
  return () => ++n;
}
const next = counter();
console.log(next(), next()); // 1 2
~~~

The returned function keeps access to n even after counter has returned. It captures a binding, not a fresh integer copied for every invocation.

## 3. Microtasks are processed before the next timer task

~~~js
console.log("A");
setTimeout(() => console.log("C"), 0);
Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log("B"));
// A, B, C
~~~

The synchronous print runs first; the fulfilled Promise continuation is a microtask; the timer callback is queued for a later task. A zero delay does not mean immediate execution.

## 4. Async functions yield a Promise

~~~js
async function answer() { return 42; }
answer().then(console.log); // 42
~~~

An async function returning a plain number still produces a Promise that resolves to the number. It does not turn CPU-intensive loops into work on another thread.

## 5. The receiver and lexical this are different

~~~js
const user = {
  name: "Ada",
  greet() { return this.name; },
};
console.log(user.greet()); // Ada
~~~

A normal method uses the receiver at call time. An arrow function captures this lexically; it does not receive a new this from the object property to which it happens to be assigned.

## 6. Prototypes supply inherited properties

~~~js
const proto = { speak() { return "hello"; } };
const user = Object.create(proto);
console.log(user.speak()); // hello
~~~

Property lookup checks the object, then its prototype chain. Prototypes are not copied into every object.

**Official reference:** [ECMAScript specification](https://tc39.es/ecma262/), [MDN JavaScript Guide](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide).
